main.title: Tetris Effect
main.summary: Tetris Effect is a block-dropping arcade-styled puzzle video game developed by Japanese studios Monstars and Resonair and published by Enhance Games.

cards.heading: The PS4 debut and virtual reality
cards.text: Tetris Effect is a block-dropping arcade-styled puzzle video game developed by Japanese studios Monstars and Resonair and published by Enhance Games. The game was released worldwide exclusively for the PlayStation 4 on November 9, 2018, and features support for the PlayStation VR. A Microsoft Windows version, with support for Oculus Rift and HTC Vive, was released exclusively on the Epic Games Store on July 23, 2019. A version for the Meta Quest standalone VR headset was released on May 14, 2020.

cards.heading: From Tetris Effect to Connected
cards.text: The game garnered high praise from critics and was named Game of the Year by several publications. An enhanced version, named Tetris Effect: Connected, was announced for Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S and Windows 10 during Xbox Games Showcase on July 23, 2020, and was released on November 10, 2020. The expansion was made available for existing platforms in August 2021. Versions for Nintendo Switch and Amazon Luna were released in October 2021 and August 2022, respectively. A PlayStation 5 version, with support for the PlayStation VR2, was released on February 22, 2023.

main.title: Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!
main.subtitle: Kanto with a partner at the player’s side
main.summary: Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee! are Game Freak's Switch reimaginings of Pokémon Yellow, released on 16 November 2018.

cards.heading: Kanto with a partner at the player’s side
cards.text: Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee! are Game Freak's Switch reimaginings of Pokémon Yellow, released on 16 November 2018. The player returns to Kanto with Pikachu or Eevee as a close companion, collecting Pokémon and challenging Trainers and Gym Leaders. The familiar landscape is presented around creatures visibly moving in the environment. Choosing which one to approach becomes part of exploration, while the partner traveling beside the player gives the two versions a personal relationship at the center of the larger collection.

cards.heading: A different way to catch wild Pokémon
cards.text: Wild encounters use a catching system influenced by Pokémon Go. Berries and timed Poké Ball throws replace the usual battle against an ordinary wild Pokémon, while Trainer battles retain the party's turn-based attacks. Joy-Con gestures or the optional Poké Ball Plus connect the throw to a physical action. A second person can join with another controller and assist in encounters and battles. The design creates different kinds of cooperation: the Pokémon party works within the battle, and another player can help guide the journey from outside it.

cards.heading: A bridge between two kinds of journey
cards.text: Pikachu or Eevee can be dressed up and signals nearby hidden items, while other Pokémon can follow or carry the player through Kanto. Connectivity with Pokémon Go brings another route into the collection. Junichi Masuda directed the games, and Shota Kageyama arranged their music. The release sought both returning players and newcomers, joining a recognizable early adventure to the catching gestures many had learned on a phone. It made Kanto another meeting point between the series' long console history and its much wider mobile audience.

main.title: Golden Joystick Awards 2018
main.summary: The Golden Joystick Awards, with every category winner of the 2018 edition.

cards.heading: The players' awards
cards.text: The Golden Joystick Awards celebrate games through a public vote, bringing players into the choice of each year's winners. The awards began in Britain with the 1983 season and later reached an international audience through online voting. Their changing categories trace the growth of games: home computers and consoles, handhelds, online play, independent studios, performance and music. Alongside the public vote, special honours recognise individual contributions to the industry. Each edition preserves its own category names, so the results also show what players and the awards organisers considered worth celebrating at the time.

main.title: Battlefield V
main.subtitle: Squads and individual stories in the Second World War
main.summary: Battlefield V returns DICE’s military shooter series to the Second World War, combining large multiplayer battles with short single-player War Stories. Electronic Arts released it on 20 November 2018 for PC, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One.

cards.heading: Battlefield returns to the Second World War
cards.text: Developed by DICE and published by Electronic Arts, Battlefield V arrived on PC, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One on 20 November 2018. After Battlefield 1 explored the First World War, its successor returned to the Second World War. The game combines infantry, vehicles and destructible environments, with large multiplayer battles alongside a collection of shorter single-player stories.

cards.heading: Squads shape the battle
cards.text: Multiplayer places particular emphasis on squads and limited resources. Players support each other with supplies and revives, while the Company system offers character, weapon and cosmetic customization. Grand Operations links several stages into a larger campaign: each round has its own objectives, and the outcome influences the next stage rather than treating every battle as an isolated match.

cards.heading: War Stories follow different perspectives
cards.text: The single-player War Stories present different wartime perspectives. Under No Flag follows a British sabotage mission in North Africa; Nordlys centres on Norwegian resistance; Tirailleur follows Senegalese soldiers fighting in France. A fourth episode, The Last Tiger, arrived in December 2018 and follows a German tank crew near the end of the war. These episodes complement the scale of multiplayer with individual stories.

main.title: Persona Q2: New Cinema Labyrinth
main.subtitle: The Phantom Thieves enter the cinema
main.summary: Persona Q2: New Cinema Labyrinth is Atlus' Nintendo 3DS dungeon role-playing crossover bringing Persona 5's Phantom Thieves together with characters from Persona 3 and Persona 4. Trapped around a mysterious cinema, the assembled cast explores labyrinths based on the films being screened. The setting gives each expedition a different fictional world while the theatre provides a place to return. First-person exploration, drawn maps and turn-based battles connect the new film premise with the dungeon structure established by the earlier Persona Q adventure on the same handheld.

cards.heading: The Phantom Thieves enter the cinema
cards.text: Persona Q2: New Cinema Labyrinth is Atlus' Nintendo 3DS dungeon role-playing crossover bringing Persona 5's Phantom Thieves together with characters from Persona 3 and Persona 4. Trapped around a mysterious cinema, the assembled cast explores labyrinths based on the films being screened. The setting gives each expedition a different fictional world while the theatre provides a place to return. First-person exploration, drawn maps and turn-based battles connect the new film premise with the dungeon structure established by the earlier Persona Q adventure on the same handheld.

cards.heading: Map the film from the inside
cards.text: Exploration presents the party's viewpoint on the upper screen and a developing map below. Players can record the layout themselves or use automatic mapping support, marking useful details as routes become familiar. Random battles share the labyrinths with visible, powerful enemies whose presence must be considered while moving through the space. Party members use both their own Personas and additional sub-Personas, giving preparation several layers. Choosing who enters a film affects the available abilities, while the map preserves what the player has learned about its physical arrangement.

cards.heading: A larger cast needs time together
cards.text: Special Screenings provide additional encounters and interactions between characters from the different original games. Completing them can unlock combined abilities, giving those meetings a practical connection with the battle system. The cinema setting allows familiar personalities to meet outside their usual stories, while the films provide a succession of shared problems. The large cast makes party selection part of the crossover's appeal. A return to the theatre offers another opportunity to change the group, follow a new interaction and see how a different combination approaches the next expedition.

main.title: The Game Awards
main.subtitle: A shared archive of the work we remember
main.summary: A celebration of game makers, with every category winner from 2014 onward.

cards.heading: What the awards celebrate
cards.text: The Game Awards celebrates the people who make games: designers, artists, writers, performers, composers and the teams around them. Created by Geoff Keighley in 2014, the annual show combines awards with performances, announcements and conversations about the medium.

cards.heading: A changing medium, a shared stage
cards.text: An awards archive is also a record of changing priorities. Categories make room for new ways to play and new kinds of work, from independent production and performance to accessibility and community support. Move through the years to read every category winner, then open the official ceremony beside the list.
